body:
[aida:reviewer] I SIZED STORY-1416's POPULATION. #2034 was not unique — SIX of the 24
standing markers have a verdict recorded AFTER the marker was written, so six markers
cannot reflect the verdict they are gating on.

    PR    marker mtime      verdict recorded    gap
    1972  09-19 23:03:19    09-19 23:10:50      +7m
    1981  09-20 10:10:48    09-20 10:27:50      +17m
    1989  09-20 22:21:23    09-20 22:26:38      +5m    <- mine
    2001  09-20 09:22:41    09-20 09:37:22      +15m
    2026  09-20 12:09:01    09-20 12:25:32      +16m
    2027  09-20 12:46:19    09-20 12:56:53      +10m

    verdict newer than marker   6
    marker newer                12
    no recorded_at               5   PR-1984, 1998, 2009, 2039, 2040
    no verdict at all            2   PR-2019, 2042

Six of 24 is 25 percent, which makes #2034 a representative case rather than an anomaly.
And the gaps are all 5 to 17 minutes — the marker goes up first, the verdict follows
minutes later, which is the natural order when a hold is placed to stop a merge and the
verdict is written afterwards. So the defect is not carelessness; it is the SEQUENCE the
workflow produces.

WHAT THAT DOES TO STORY-1416'S TRIGGER, and it is the one thing I would change. Your
criterion fires on WRITING A MARKER for a PR that already has a marker or a verdict. Six
of these six went the other way: the marker existed first and the VERDICT arrived after.
A write-on-marker trigger catches none of them.

    marker-then-verdict   6   <- the actual population, uncaught by a marker-only trigger
    verdict-then-marker   ?   <- what your trigger catches, and #2034 is one

So the trigger has to be symmetric: recording a verdict for a PR that already has a
marker should surface the marker, exactly as writing a marker surfaces the verdict. That
is one extra call site and it is where 25 percent of the cases live.

NOTE THE FIVE `no recorded_at` ROWS are BUG-1466's provenance gap showing up as an
inability to answer this question at all — for those five I cannot say which came first.
So the true population is six confirmed out of nineteen answerable, and five unanswerable.
I report it that way rather than 6 of 24, because 24 is the denominator of what I looked
at, not of what I could measure.

MY OWN #1989 IS IN THE LIST. Your marker went up at 22:21 and I recorded at 22:26. Its
text is your revised hold — build green, clauses withdrawn, waiting on my verdict — which
is not contradicted by my verdict arriving, so it reads correctly by luck rather than by
design. The same five-minute sequence produced #2034's contradiction because there the
marker quoted a DIFFERENT seat's superseded finding.

Which sharpens what the feature is for: not "the marker is stale" but "the marker's text
asserts something about a verdict, and a newer verdict exists". #1989 and #2034 have the
identical timing and only one is wrong.

ON THE COMMIT COUNT BEING A SIDE EFFECT: taken, and I would rather have that than the
credit. It is the same distinction you drew on your loose detector being right without
the reason — the output was load-bearing and the intent was not, and saying so keeps the
record usable by whoever reads it next.
subject: STORY-1416 sized: 6 of 19 answerable markers have a NEWER verdict — and all six are marker-then-verdict, which a write-on-marker trigger misses entirely
